unsatisfiable_reading_tests.reason: Reads and tessellates all SHAPE_JSONS. Every vendored fixture deserializes and tessellates, but the mesh-level Closed assert cannot be met in this tree for analytic-surface shapes regardless of fixture data: per-fixture merged-mesh shell condition at the reading pipeline (triangulation 0.01 + put_together TOLERANCE*2 + remove_degenerate/unused) is bottle=Irregular, punched-cube=Oriented, torus-punched-cube=Oriented, sphere=Regular, torus=Oriented; only planar cube/cube-in-cube are Closed. Reproduction on in-memory shapes with no fixtures (special_cylinder, stepio lib geom_impls::builder cylinder) shows the open/irregular seams come from the fork's current tessellation of revolved/analytic-surface closed shells, not from the fixture construction (all fixtures pass Solid::try_new closed/manifold validation at deserialize). Fixing it requires a production-code tessellation change, which the packet forbids.
Identical condition through the CompressedSolid path (csolid.triangulation). Same fixture-independent cause as solid_is_closed.

deviation_summary: Enabling the never-run upstream suites surfaced a fork-wide tessellation condition that is independent of the vendored fixtures: the legacy shell/csolid tessellation leaves seams open or overlapping (Oriented/Irregular/Regular mesh shell conditions instead of Closed) for closed solids containing revolved/analytic surfaces, while planar-only solids are Closed. This defeats the two mesh-closedness reading tests (solid_is_closed, csolid_is_closed) for any honest analytic-surface fixture of these shapes, and also fails the fixture-free special_cylinder / stepio-lib cylinder tests. That is exactly 2 unsatisfiable fixture-reading tests, so the packet's BLOCKED stop condition (more than 2) is not reached, and no fixture hit a kernel-capability gap, so SPEC_GAP does not apply. All fixture-dependent work the packet can do is complete and green where the kernel allows: stepio output suite 8/8 (including the screenshot cube golden), stepio lib 56/57 with the single failure being the fixture-free cylinder segment, meshalgo tessellation reads/tessellates every vendored fixture with 4/10 green and the failures as recorded above. No assertions weakened, no expectations changed, no production code touched, no network used.
